name: Northern Mariana Islands

findings.summary: After Typhoon Soudelor, IT&E chose Ericsson to upgrade its radio and core network on Saipan, launch its first 4G LTE network there, and more than double HSPA capacity on Saipan, Rota and Tinian; equipment began arriving August 2015.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor rule: Ericsson supplies RAN and core, so pole third. Tier 4 because the release reports equipment delivery under way, not confirmed operation at scale. Single opened S1 vendor release, hence medium. Pre-2020 and not reconfirmed as current; whether IT&E's later 5G (with SK Telecom engineering support, 2019) still runs on Ericsson is unknown.

findings.local_actor: Docomo Pacific (lead/owner); CNMI and Guam governments (2016 agreement parties)
findings.summary: Docomo Pacific began laying the NEC-built ATISA submarine fibre cable in May 2017, linking Guam with Saipan, Tinian and Rota, with a Saipan landing ceremony on 11 May and full service expected by August 2017.
findings.analyst_inference: Equipment vendor rule: NEC built the cable, so pole third. Tier 4 (marine lay under way); ready-for-service was only expected, not confirmed, in sources opened. Both articles appear to derive from Docomo Pacific's announcement, so independence is weak. Docomo Pacific is NTT Docomo-owned (Japan), but as owner-operator it does not set the pole of equipment. Saipan Tribune page showed no year; dated via Ocean News.
